en: For all of us back then, all we wanted was to see you go to Koshien.

But that dream was about to be shattered by the opposing
school. And only I had the muscle to protect it.
For me, protecting that dream was the same as protecting my own.
I can kind of understand, but that got you expelled and landed you in juvie.
Did you really have to make that big a sacrifice?
This may sound sentimental, but people do entrust their dreams to others.

They lay down what they couldn't achieve on their own, and
offer it to someone who can.

By watching that person march forward, carrying a bright new
future on their shoulders...
They can accept their own reality and live their own lives...
Thinking that one day, they too might be able to make their own dreams come true.
I had no dream of my own back then.

Despite that, I knew I could at least help someone else reach
their full potential.

I was already destined to take over the family business.
Graduating was the least of my concerns.
It was more important to help the team get to Koshien. Everyone's hopes were riding on it.
I'll never forget the moment when your home run cleared the stadium.

Even now, thinking back on it gives me the motivation to
keep moving forward, even when the road ahead seems grim.
Tatsuo, you have no idea how grateful I am to you.
Dojima-kun, that family business of yours...

I'm the Tojo Clan's sixth chairman. Although I'm currently
off their radar for the time being.
That's why I need to handle this. It's too risky for a civilian like you to get in any deeper.
You gave everyone enough to dream about. It's my turn to help you regain the one you lost.
What do you mean...?
When everything is said and done, I'll have the major leagues rescind your permanent ban.
And if you can't return as a player, I'll negotiate your return as either a coach or manager.
But for now, use that money to get your affairs in order.

Don't worry. I have more going for me now than just
brute strength. I'll rewind those 15 years you lost.
So, the Nagoya Family was never a true yakuza organization.
It came into existence 15 years ago as a neighborhood watch to protect local interests.
Right. And the one controlling the Nagoya Family ever since...
Was the same person managing me and the rest of the Wyverns⑬Fujita-san.
Back then, the town was split east and west between the Tojo Clan and the Omi Alliance.
They both ran match-fixing rackets to supplement their baseball betting, all of which depended on the Wyverns.
So your expulsion was all part of Fujita's scheme to drive off the Tojo and the Omi...
Clearing them out of Nagoya was his true objective.
After Fujita-san resigned as manager, he kept the truth hidden.
At the same time, he made it seem like the Nagoya Family was a legitimate yakuza gang to keep any real yakuza groups from moving in.
It's like they were a secret society or a mafia or something.
But, that all ended yesterday. The Nagoya Family was well organized, but its members were still just regular citizens.
Now that their secret's out, they're powerless.
What about your attackers?
They all turned themselves in this morning.
Ushijima-san and Milky-chan⑬the two who looked after me the most⑬persuaded the rest to do it.
For 15 years, they harbored their secret in silence, dreading that this day would come.
That must have been difficult for you.
Well, yeah. But I can't go feeling sorry for myself.
Not until I find the real enemy who's behind all this.
Last night, when Ushijima-san and the others captured me, I knew for sure.
These guys weren't killers.
It's true they were acting on Fujita-san's orders, but they're not capable of staging the accidents which happened over the past few days.
You mean Sakai's death at the construction site?

That's not all. I nearly lost my life several times as soon
as I started looking into the Nagoya Family.

I'm sure the recent deaths of the Tojo and Omi officers were
part of their grand scheme, too.
Ushijima-san and the others were part of the Nagoya Family, sure.

But they hesitated to even raise a fist at me. Murder would
be completely out of the question for them.
There have to be actual criminals behind this.

Let me get this straight. This so-called Nagoya Family is a
front for an actual, more sinister yakuza group?
I see. Then I know a man who's involved. It has to be him...
What man? You know who's pulling Fujita-san's strings?

I've been investigating the Nagoya Family to see whether
the guy I'm thinking of is linked to this or not.
But it looks like I'll need to hear the rest from Fujita himself.
Well done. Your pay, as promised.
Your job's over. I'm going back to Tokyo. I suggest you clear your debts and think about finding a new line of work.
Hold on a second. Are you gonna go meet Fujita-san?
Then count me in on this. I've got some questions of my own for him!
You're late.
ctx: diálogo uid01330403 + frase de acompañante/calle STID_ST_FUKUOKA

en: Ahahah... My bad.
We don't have much time. Let's hear it.
Okay. I'm not sure where to start...
(It's morning... Man, feels like I slept for years.)
(Oh, right. I have to report to that guy.)
I have something important to tell you.
Wait. I'll hear it in person. I take it you're at home? Then I'll be over.
(I'm sure he'll take his sweet time... Maybe I'll step out for a bit?)
Hey, sorry. Didn't mean to keep you.
Are you done now?
Yup. Let's do this.
Hey, where are you?
Oh, sorry. I stepped out for a bit. I'll be back right away.
I'm not playing games here. Hurry back.
(Uh-oh. Better mosey on home with a spring in my step.)
Sawada.
I had a feeling you would know to find me here.
Good on you, Shinada.

I saw the evening paper. Never would've expected the
league's top pitcher to get traded to the Wyverns,
the eternal underdog.
It was my promise to Fujita-san. That I would take his place in 15 years.
I didn't realize Fujita-san's return to baseball would mean a new boss for the Nagoya Family.
Am I wrong, Sawada?
You are aware this is my hometown, right?
Yup. The ace of Chukyo Academy, the genius of Nagoya. You had plenty of nicknames in high school.
But life can be strange, can't it? By the luck of the draw, my career ended up in Tokyo.
While you, a Tokyo native, joined the ranks of Nagoya's elites.
As a result, you had your career stolen for Nagoya's sake. A place with no connection to you.
While I became the league's undisputed ace.
But now you're back in Nagoya.
Are you doing this to inherit the Nagoya Family from Fujita-san?
Why? Why do you need to go so far to protect the Nagoya Family!?
Isn't there something else you should be protecting instead!?
A friend from high school once told me... that people like us help others to dream.
You and I do more than just play some game here!
The players who stand on this field carry the dreams of all sorts of people!

You've heard, haven't you? Ushijima-san, Manabe-san...
The entire Nagoya Family has turned itself in.
Sawada, the Nagoya Family is finished. Let me put it to you straight.
I want you to stop causing any more suffering using the Nagoya Family.
Apparently you're blind to what's really going on.
I know the Nagoya Family is finished.
I came back to Nagoya to finish one last job.

What else? To get rid of the guy who's got the most dirt on
the Nagoya Family.
That was my final task.
Everyone who turned themselves in this morning has been released. No one will be pressing any charges.
How is that⑬
Shinada, this thing is controlled by someone far more powerful than you can imagine.

Someone with the power to play the police like puppets.
That's what you're up against.
You're just being used, Sawada. Who's doing this? Who's really aiming that gun!?
Over there.
Who are they?
ctx: diálogo uid01330417 + frase de acompañante/calle STID_ST_KAMURO

en: My observers. From the Omi Alliance.
The Omi? Why them?
That's your answer. Fujita-san and I, we were used by a faction within the Omi Alliance.
A faction?
An offshoot from Kobe. The Kuroha Family.
The Nagoya Family was constructed as a puppet organization for the Kuroha Family to drive out the Omi Alliance and take their piece of the pie.
In other words, it's part of an internal schism within the Omi Alliance.
Just so one Omi group could drive out another Omi group?
And both Coach Fujita and I sold our souls to the Kuroha Family to make our dreams come true.
Shinada, I was never the genius or the baseball hero you thought I was.
Even way back at Koshien... I only won the nationals with the Kuroha's help.
That can't be...
It is. The Kuroha bribed coaches from other schools and threatened their players.
They did anything possible so I could win.
Wait, so the goons from Kamuro Tech who threatened us before the regional final...
That's right. The Kuroha's doing.
Of course, some punk from your school had to go screw up the plan.
So our first-round game against each other was your only real match.
No wonder I didn't notice.
For me, the Koshien tournament was only real in the first round. That match was essentially the final.
The pure, unbridled slugging machine, Tatsuo Shinada. All I had to do was hold you off one game, and we'd have that tournament in the bag.
I'd say I did that and then some.
I kicked you out of nationals first round, which got you buried in the draft to the Wyverns.

Whereas I was considered the pinnacle of high school
baseball and signed with the Gigants as their first pick.
Can you guess why the Kuroha Family went so far to make me win the nationals?
Oh yes. They did it to enable match fixing in every single game I pitched between the Gigants and the Wyverns.
It was completely undetectable, and nothing was swayed by chance. The Kuroha gained complete and utter control of baseball betting.
That's crazy...
Baseball betting is a tough thing to manage. It's not easy to fix a game.
You can pay off a pitcher, but if the opposing batters don't score, you can't force a win.
You can pay off the batters, but if the opponents don't score, you can't force a loss.

But the Wyvern's starting lineup and manager were in on it.
And if they face me as the opposing pitcher...
...Then fixing matches would practically be child's play.
That was the idea. But even though it was nearly flawless, it failed just once.
That game where you hit your home run, Shinada.

The Kuroha Family's order was for the home team,
the Wyverns, to lose with a 1-0 score.
But, at the bottom of the ninth, the Gigants didn't have a run to their name.
Even if they wanted us to win, there was nothing they could do if our batters couldn't score.
And using a blatant error to get our team ahead would've looked bad in front of the cameras.
So Coach Fujita replaced Sakai on second with you, a guy with no major league experience, to pinch hit.
That means Coach Fujita thought I couldn't get a hit off of you?
He knew your strengths and weaknesses better than anyone.
That's why he instructed you to keep throwing curveballs at me?
But then, that seventh pitch. Why'd you change to a fastball?
Did you ignore orders just so you could settle our showdown, Sawada?
No. That was definitely Fujita-san's order.
What? That was his call...?

That's right. I was instructed to throw that fastball
by none other than Coach Fujita. Make no mistake.
Why? Why would he do that!?
Because...

(Uh-oh, is that Uno-san? If he spots me, I'll never hear the
end of it. Gonna have to find another way.)
(This would be the long way around. Gotta hurry my ass to Futo Momo.)
(Gotta hustle back to Futo Momo. I'm running out of time here...)
(Milky-chan's brother's in trouble. I need to get to... Kubota Security? I think that's where it was.)
(Gotta submit this text to the publisher. Heading down Kume Boulevard would be the quickest way.)

(No matter where I go, it won't change the fact that I'm
broke. The batting center's the only option I have left.)
(It's about time I sent something back to Morning Glory. I'm thinking 10,000 yen at least... I know how much they need it.)
(There. May your new shoes carry you wherever you want to go in life.)
(I remember her being pretty quick on her feet. Heh. It was all I could do to keep up with her.)
(Although she's the quiet, precocious type, she actually seems pretty athletic.)
(We eventually convinced her to join the track team. I hear she's a long-distance runner now, and quite good at it.)
(She's also caring and committed, but I worry she doesn't put herself first often enough. She needs to learn to take it easy sometimes.)
